fbcover.content.h1: What is the Facebook Cover Photo Resizer and Why Do You Need It?
fbcover.content.p1a: Your Facebook cover photo is the visual billboard of your personal profile, business page, community group, or event. It is the very first thing people see when they visit your Facebook presence. However, getting your cover photo to look great on every device is notoriously challenging because Facebook displays cover photos differently on computer monitors and smartphone screens.
fbcover.content.p1b: On desktop computers, Facebook stretches your cover wide (820 × 312 pixels) and cuts off the top and bottom. On smartphones, Facebook displays the cover taller (640 × 360 pixels) and cuts off the left and right sides. Without proper resizing and safe-zone positioning, important logos, text, or faces get cut off. ImgFeel's free Facebook Cover Photo Resizer solves this permanently by framing your image to the exact 1640 × 720 px high-DPI resolution with live dual safe-zone guides.
fbcover.content.feat1Desc: Automatically resizes any photo to the optimal 1640 × 720 px master resolution so it renders crisp and clear on both phones and computers.
fbcover.content.feat2Desc: Keep critical headlines, logos, and focal points inside the golden safe zone so Facebook never cuts them off during display.
fbcover.content.feat3Desc: Fit tall vertical photos or square images seamlessly without cutting off the subject by adding an ambient frosted blur backdrop.
fbcover.content.feat4Desc: All resizing, cropping, and canvas rendering happens completely inside your web browser. Your private photos are never uploaded or saved to any server.

fbcover.content.h3: Official Facebook Cover Photo Dimensions & Sizes (2026 Guide)
fbcover.content.p3a: Here are the exact dimensions you need for every type of Facebook cover and banner in 2026:
fbcover.content.spec1Desc: Master Resolution: 1640 × 720 px (Recommended). Desktop Display: 820 × 312 px. Mobile Display: 640 × 360 px. Aspect Ratio: 16:9 on mobile, ~2.63:1 on desktop.
fbcover.content.spec2Desc: Recommended Size: 1640 × 856 px (Aspect Ratio: 1.91:1). On mobile devices, Facebook crops approximately 96 pixels off the top and bottom.
fbcover.content.spec3Desc: Recommended Size: 1200 × 628 px (Aspect Ratio: 1.91:1). Ideal for public events, concerts, webinars, business workshops, and party announcements.
fbcover.content.spec4Desc: Use PNG for graphics, text, and logos to avoid compression artifacts. Use JPG for complex portraits and landscape photos. Keep file size under 500 KB.
fbcover.content.h4: Understanding the Safe Zone: How to Stop Facebook from Cutting Off Content
fbcover.content.p4a: The Facebook Safe Zone is the central area of your cover photo that is guaranteed to display on both computer monitors and mobile phone screens. Here is how to master it:
fbcover.content.sz1Desc: Place your brand name, slogan, contact details, and key faces within the central safe area (820 × 312 px). This ensures nothing gets clipped on any screen.
fbcover.content.sz2Desc: On personal profiles and business pages, your circular profile photo overlaps the bottom-left corner of the cover photo. Keep all important text toward the center or right.
fbcover.content.sz3Desc: Our tool generates live simulated mockups of both desktop pages and the mobile Facebook app in real time so you can inspect cropping before downloading.
fbcover.content.h5: 5 Pro Tips for Creating an Engaging, High-Converting Facebook Cover
fbcover.content.p5a: Make your Facebook page look professional and drive more followers and customers with these proven design principles:
fbcover.content.tip1Desc: Don't overcrowd your banner. Use a single bold headline that communicates who you are, what you offer, or what problem you solve in under 3 seconds.
fbcover.content.tip2Desc: Ensure your text stands out strongly against the background image. If the photo is busy or bright, use a subtle dark tint or bold high-contrast fonts.
fbcover.content.tip3Title: Direct Attention to Your Action Button
fbcover.content.tip3Desc: Use directional arrows or subtle design lines to draw visitor eyes toward your page's action button (e.g., 'Message Us', 'Shop Now', or 'Follow').
fbcover.content.tip4Desc: Facebook heavily compresses uploaded media. Exporting at 2x Retina resolution (1640 × 720 px) ensures your cover looks razor-sharp on high-density smartphone screens.
fbcover.content.tip5Desc: Keep your cover photo fresh by updating it regularly for seasonal promotions, new product launches, holiday greetings, or major community milestones.
fbcover.content.h6: Common Mistakes to Avoid When Making a Facebook Cover Photo
fbcover.content.p6a: Avoid these frequent pitfalls to keep your Facebook banner looking polished and credible:
fbcover.content.mistake1Desc: Over 85% of Facebook users browse on mobile phones. Designing only for desktop widescreen results in text on the sides getting cut off on phones.
fbcover.content.mistake2Title: Placing Information in the Bottom-Left Corner
fbcover.content.mistake2Desc: Placing phone numbers, websites, or key faces in the lower-left corner means they will be blocked by your circular profile avatar.
fbcover.content.mistake3Desc: Stretching small images creates ugly pixelation and distortion. Always start with a high-resolution image and use our tool to frame it cleanly.
fbcover.content.mistake4Desc: Paragraphs and small fonts become unreadable on mobile screens. Keep text short, large, and easy to read at a glance.
fbcover.content.faq1Q: What is the best size for a Facebook cover photo in 2026?
fbcover.content.faq1A: The optimal master resolution is 1640 × 720 pixels (or 820 × 360 px at standard density). This resolution accounts for both desktop (820 × 312 px) and mobile (640 × 360 px) screens without quality loss.
fbcover.content.faq2Q: Why does Facebook cut off the sides or top of my cover photo?
fbcover.content.faq2A: Facebook displays cover photos in different aspect ratios depending on the device. On computers, it displays widescreen (820 × 312 px) and crops the top and bottom. On smartphones, it displays taller (640 × 360 px) and crops the left and right sides.
fbcover.content.faq3Q: How do I fit a vertical or square photo into a Facebook cover without cropping?
fbcover.content.faq3A: Choose the 'Fit Full Image (Blurred Backdrop)' preset in our tool. It keeps your entire original photo centered and fills the empty widescreen sides with a stylish ambient frosted blur backdrop.
fbcover.content.faq4Q: What size should a Facebook Group cover photo be?
fbcover.content.faq4A: Facebook Group covers should be 1640 × 856 pixels (a 1.91:1 aspect ratio). Facebook crops approximately 96 pixels from the top and bottom on mobile devices.
fbcover.content.faq5Q: What size should a Facebook Event cover banner be?
fbcover.content.faq5A: The recommended size for a Facebook Event banner is 1200 × 628 pixels (1.91:1 ratio), which scales cleanly across the desktop event page and mobile news feeds.
fbcover.content.faq6Q: Why is my Facebook cover photo blurry after uploading?
fbcover.content.faq6A: Facebook heavily compresses images that exceed 100 KB or have incorrect aspect ratios. To prevent blur, export your cover at 1640 × 720 px as a PNG file (for text/graphics) or high-quality JPG (under 500 KB).
